newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian post, phone workers end week-long strike.
newsitem.headline: Indian post, phone workers end week-long strike.

text.p: Indian postal and telephone workers on Tuesday called off a week-long strike after the government decided to lift a ceiling on bonus payments, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
The news agency quoted O.P. Gupta, head of the National Federation of Telecom Employees (NFTE) saying, workers would resume duty on Wednesday.
Indian Telecommunications Minister Beni Prasad Varma earlier announced the decision to lift the bonus ceiling prompting the unions to call off their strike.
About one million postal and telephone workers in India went on strike last week against a government decision to impose a 3,500 rupees ($100) ceiling on annual pay bonuses.
The ceiling was imposed as an austerity measure by the federal government earlier this year.
But the post and telephone workers argued that a bonus ceiling for railway workers had already been lifted and set a precedent.
Millions of letters have piled up as a result of the strike by six trade unions, three of them representing postal unions.
Telephone workers had stopped manual services like repairs and billing in telephone exchanges but most telephones were working because of automated exchanges.
